## Segment summary
This segment documents the progression of building an AI robot named "AI BUDDY" over Day 2, showcasing its evolution from a simple talking device (version 1) to a more advanced model (version 1.5) with object and face tracking capabilities. The creator, Aykhan, demonstrates the robot's new features, including its ability to observe its surroundings, track faces and held objects, and perform body movements using SG90 servos. The segment also shows the assembly process and the components used, like the ESP32S3 CAM.

<0:02.0> - The robot head is shown being held by a hand, demonstrating its size and portability.
<0:04.0> - A hand holds up a smaller, older version of the robot, labeled "version 1," with a different display.

## Audio summary

A male speaker with an English accent, likely in his twenties, is discussing building a custom AI body for a character named Mac. The conversation focuses on the physical components used, such as server motors, a camera, and various parts, as well as the time spent assembling them. There is no music or background sound present in this clip.
## Speech

The speaker says, 'my name is ikehan and this is mac. mac was only able to talk to me, so i gave him a new body now we can observe everything around him track my face and whatever i'm holding for body movements, i use two server motors and the camera from e sp32 s3. i spent a lot of time putting all together because i didn't know that there were gonna be so many ways.'

## Segment summary
A person is shown building and programming a small robot, referred to as "Mac," using a computer. The segment begins with the physical assembly of the robot's hardware, followed by the use of an AI tool called "Cursor" to simultaneously develop multiple software components for the robot, including its movement logic and a website interface. The final frames show the robot's face display being controlled in real-time by a software interface, and conclude with a call to action for viewers to comment "MINIBOT" for a project link.

- 0:21.4 - A hand holds a small, white 3D-printed robot head with wires attached, showing the hardware assembly.
- 0:24.7 - The person is shown sitting at a desk, working on a computer after completing the hardware build.
- 0:28.7 - The person opens the "Cursor" software application on the computer.
- 0:32.7 - The person starts multiple agents within the Cursor application to work on different parts of the project simultaneously.
- 0:34.7 - One agent is shown working on the movement logic for the robot, with the robot's physical hardware displayed on screen.
- 0:36.7 - Another agent is shown working on the face tracking and website design for the robot's OLED screen.
- 0:40.7 - The robot's face display is shown updating in real-time to reflect different expressions as selected in the "face deck" software interface.
- 0:42.1 - The video ends with a static shot of the person typing on the keyboard, overlaid with a call to action.
